column1: # The DEFAULT is that every case runs on every axis (jit, aot-o0, aot-o2,
# vm-src, vm-eskb) and must match its hand-authored golden. This file is the
# only way to exempt a (case, axis) pair, and every row needs a justification,
# so an engine losing a `guard` form has to be written down rather than
# quietly dropped. scripts/run_guard_coverage.sh fails on a row naming a case
# or axis that does not exist (a stale waiver) and on a row with no
#   axis  — jit | aot-o0 | aot-o2 | vm-src | vm-eskb

column4: The VM's `error` is a fixed 1-argument native (fid 237) and its error-object-irritants always answers '(): a divergence already filed upstream at tests/vm_parity/found/error_object_irritants_empty.esk. error-object? / -message / the empty-irritants case are all required on this axis and pass, in 06_error_objects.esk; only the variadic-irritant checks are exempt here.
Same VM `error` arity limit as the vm-src row above; the ESKB route runs the same native. See tests/vm_parity/found/error_object_irritants_empty.esk.

A `set!` to a top-level binding from inside a guard CLAUSE body does not reach that binding on the VM: the handler is its own closure frame and the write lands there. Silent - the clause still returns the right value. Repro found/vm_setbang_global_from_guard_clause_lost.esk, ledger SW-85. Both native axes are required and pass.
Same VM binding defect as the vm-src row; the ESKB route compiles the same handler-as-closure shape. See found/vm_setbang_global_from_guard_clause_lost.esk (SW-85).
Internal `define`s in a guard BODY do not yield the body's value on the VM. Repro found/vm_internal_defines_in_guard_body.esk, ledger SW-86. Both native axes are required and pass.
Same as the vm-src row. See found/vm_internal_defines_in_guard_body.esk (SW-86).

The ESKB route runs the guard clause body before the dynamic-wind after-thunk, inverting the R7RS order. vm-src and all three native axes agree with R7RS and are required here, so this waiver is one axis wide and is itself a native-vs-vm-src-vs-vm-eskb three-way divergence. Repro found/vm_eskb_wind_order_vs_clause.esk, ledger SW-89.

Native binds the guard variable to an SSA value rather than an alloca, so `set!` on it is rejected: "variable 'e' is not mutable". LOUD, not silent. Both VM axes are required here and pass, so this row also records that the native side is the nonconforming one. Repro found/native_setbang_on_guard_variable_rejected.esk, ledger SW-87.
Same native binding limitation as the jit row. See found/native_setbang_on_guard_variable_rejected.esk (SW-87).
